subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 19, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 19, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS community,

We hope this newsletter finds you well. As we continue to work on improving our Linux distribution, we wanted to take a moment to highlight some recent developments and updates.

Firstly, we're excited to announce that Systemtap 5.6 has been released, bringing with it new features such as BPF LSM hooks and XDP packet-processing probes for the --bpf runtime, as well as BTF-based kernel support. This update is now available for our users to enjoy.

In addition to this, we've issued security updates for Friday, which include patches for various packages such as .NET 10.0, coreutils, kernel, libevent, libsoup3, microcode_ctl, perl-Net-DNS, postgresql18, postgresql:16, postgresql:18, tomcat, and more. These updates are essential for ensuring the security and stability of our distribution.

We've also been working on some behind-the-scenes improvements, including updating our intelligence sync to include the newsletter, archive, and wiki guides. This will help us keep our documentation up-to-date and easily accessible for our users.

On the development front, we've made some changes to our CI/CD pipeline, including passing the -R flag to gh release create and fixing a block-scalar indentation issue in our release.yml file. We've also added Firefox-ublock-origin to our Xlibre build and re-triggered our GitLab mirror to fix a deploy key issue.

In the AcreetionOS-Xlibre repository, we've merged a branch to fix a geocode-glib update conflict. This ensures that our Xlibre build remains stable and secure.

We're also excited to announce that our community member, cobra3282000, has been actively contributing to our project, working on various tasks and issues. Their dedication to our community is truly appreciated, and we're grateful for their contributions.

As we continue to work on AcreetionOS, we're committed to providing a secure, private, and user-friendly Linux distribution that meets the needs of our community. We're always looking for ways to improve and expand our project, and we invite you to join us in this journey.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community. We're excited to see what the future holds for our project, and we look forward to continuing to work together to create a better Linux distribution for all.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift, Co-Lead Developers of AcreetionOS
